The rules do not automatically grant regrowing heads or a mandatory weakness to fire. The party may need to prepare a crossing, secure an escape route, and discover why the hydra moved toward a settlement. Luring it away from the road or resolving the original environmental disturbance can be a complete expedition objective.

strings.Každé kolo může zaútočit na 2 různé cíle: Each round, may attack 2 different targets; both attacks suffer −2 to their final ATTACK. Reduces the first two instances of damage it takes each round by 3 (minimum 0).

best/wyverna.name: Wyvern
profile: A wyvern is a large winged monster with a predatory body and a dangerous venomous stinger. In Elaria, it nests on cliffs, high ruins, and mountain outcrops overlooking the surrounding countryside. Remains of prey beneath its nest and marks left by large talons reveal its presence. Although it may resemble a dragon at first glance, its behavior is driven mainly by hunting and defending its own territory.

It often lives alone or in a pair with young. It is observant and can exploit favorable conditions, but this profile does not grant it a dragon's learning or a desire to build a vast hoard. It seeks food and a safe nesting place. It may attack herds if they offer easier prey than mountain animals. If it serves a person or another master, the relationship must arise from specific breeding, training, or magic.

Once per battle, Poisonous Stinger adds two damage after a physical hit, provided the base attack actually dealt damage. This is not automatically long-term poisoning or an extra attack without a condition. Height, open space, and available cover change the danger of the encounter. The party can locate the nest, prevent further attacks on herds, or help an owner recover an escaped monster. Understanding the cause of its behavior often helps choose between direct confrontation, securing the surrounding area, and changing the route.

strings.1× za souboj po fyzickém zásahu přidá 2: Once per battle, adds 2 damage after a physical hit; this bonus cannot be used if the base attack dealt 0 damage.

best/mlady-drak.name: Young Dragon
profile: A young dragon is already a very dangerous being, but is still gaining experience and establishing its own position. In Elaria, it seeks a remote lair in mountains, ruins, or deep forests, with room and supplies. It may belong to a dragon lineage that has long controlled the territory, or be an individual driven from its home. The first objects collected in its lair may reveal what it values and where it comes from.

It is intelligent and can learn from conversations and conflicts. It often acts alone, but may seek an older dragon's recognition, alliances, or servants of its own. It wants safety, food, and control over its territory. Youth may bring curiosity, pride, and poor judgment of consequences. Stealing supplies or threatening a settlement may be a calculated attempt to gain power or a reckless effort to imitate an older relative.

Once per battle, Dragon Breath allows a magical attack against up to two targets, while Dragon Scales reduces the first instance of physical damage each round. The particular dragon determines the nature of its breath; there is no need to assume that all share the same element. The party can negotiate territorial boundaries, uncover why the young dragon's behavior changed, or offer a way out of a dangerous dispute. Direct confrontation requires prepared defenses and a retreat. An agreement may be possible if the dragon sees a real benefit and need not interpret it as public humiliation.

strings.1× za souboj napadne až 2 cíle magickým: Once per battle, attacks up to 2 targets with a magical attack with a spell bonus of +3, rolling separately against each. Dragon Scales reduces the first instance of physical damage each round by 2 (minimum 0).

best/dospely-drak.name: Adult Dragon
profile: An adult dragon is an experienced, intelligent being whose presence can influence the entire surrounding territory. A lair in a mountain fortress, extensive underground chambers, or a remote ruin is more than a resting place: it may hold supplies, keepsakes, valuables, and records of old agreements. Its origins and lineage may reach back to events local people know only through legends. Its relationship with the territory is usually far longer than any individual ruler's lifetime.

It generally makes its own decisions and can plan far into the future. It may maintain servants, allies, or dependent settlements without sharing an ordinary home with other dragons. It seeks security, influence, and things it values; knowledge or a fulfilled oath may be as valuable to it as gold. Its nature varies. An adult dragon may be a destructive tyrant, a steadfast guardian of an agreement, or a being that regards short-lived human disputes as disturbances of its peace.

Once per battle, Dragon Breath can strike up to two targets. Ancient Scales reduces the first instance of physical damage and the first instance of magical damage each round. If the party discovers and actually exploits its particular weakness, this reduction stops applying and both defenses drop by two. Investigating the weakness is therefore an important part of the expedition; the particular story determines its nature, and clues must support it. An agreement, repairing a broken promise, or an offer that removes the real cause of the dragon's hostility may be equally significant.

strings.1× za souboj napadne až 2 cíle magickým: Once per battle, attacks up to 2 targets with a magical attack with a spell bonus of +4; each defends separately. Reduces the first instance of physical damage and the first instance of magical damage each round by 2. If the party discovers and actually exploits its particular weakness, this reduction does not apply and the dragon suffers −2 PDEF and MDEF.
strings.Dračí dech; Staré dračí šupiny a odhalen: Dragon Breath; Ancient Scales and Revealed Weakness

best/prastary-drak.name: Ancient Dragon
profile: An ancient dragon has survived changes to empires, landscapes, and human lineages. Its lair may be a place with its own history, extensive defenses, and objects that mattered long before today's settlements existed. In Elaria, its name may appear in chronicles in several forms because different cultures interpreted the same being differently. Its territory is usually carefully chosen, and changes in the surrounding area rarely go unnoticed.

It is highly intelligent, experienced, and generally accustomed to acting from a position of overwhelming advantage. It may rule a network of allies, influence its surroundings indirectly, or remain apart until someone disrupts its long-term plan. It seeks to preserve what it considers essential: power, memory, a promise, territory, or a particular person. Age alone means neither malice nor flawless wisdom. Long solitude and confidence in its own strength may cause it to underestimate decisions made by people whose lives seem brief to it.

Dragon Breath threatens up to two targets, while Elder Scales reduces the first instance of physical damage and the first instance of magical damage each round by three. Actually exploiting its particular weakness cancels the reduction and lowers physical and magical defense by four. Direct combat without prior investigation is therefore extraordinarily dangerous. The party can gather old accounts, discover the significance of a guarded object, and negotiate over an objective the dragon does not consider trivial. Both a weakness and the possibility of agreement need clear story clues, so success follows from understanding and preparation.

strings.1× za souboj napadne až 2 cíle magickým: Once per battle, attacks up to 2 targets with a magical attack with a spell bonus of +4; each defends separately. Reduces the first instance of physical damage and the first instance of magical damage each round by 3. If the party discovers and actually exploits its particular weakness, this reduction does not apply and the dragon suffers −4 PDEF and MDEF.
strings.Dračí dech; Prastaré dračí šupiny a odha: Dragon Breath; Elder Scales and Revealed Weakness

best/goblini-nacelnik.name: Goblin Chieftain
profile: A goblin chieftain leads a group whose safety and livelihood depend on quick decisions. The chieftain may come from a respected family, rise through cunning, or earn authority by defending the band. The leader lives in a protected part of a cave camp, ruins, or an abandoned mine. Supplies, important information, and objects others recognize as signs of rank gather around this position.

The chieftain is a more intelligent and influential opponent than a lone goblin. The leader knows the group's needs and can use both fear and the hope of reward. A chieftain may decide independently or hand over loot to a stronger patron whom the group cannot afford to disobey. Supplies, safety, and maintaining authority are central concerns. Violence toward neighbors may be a choice or the result of pressure the party does not yet understand. Relationships with guards, families, and other important goblins reveal the real foundations of the chieftain's rule.

Chieftain's Orders strengthens one goblin ally's attack each round while the chieftain is conscious. Once per battle, Cunning Dodge increases defense against a declared attack. The party can discover whose support sustains the leader, interrupt the supply of loot, or offer a solution to a shared threat. Negotiations should account for the chieftain's need to justify an agreement before the band. Defeating one leader alone may not remove the hunger, fear, or patron that caused the conflict.

strings.Dokud je při vědomí, 1 spojenec Goblin n: While conscious, one allied Goblin or Goblin Archer gains +1 to its final ATTACK each round. Once per battle, after an attack's target is declared, the chieftain gains +2 DEFENSE against that attack.

best/orci-nacelnik.name: Orc Chieftain
profile: An orc chieftain leads a group whose strength rests on warriors, supplies, and the ability to defend its territory. In Elaria, the leader may come from a respected lineage, gain leadership through a duel, or establish authority as a protector of the community. The seat of power may be a fortified camp, a mountain settlement, or an occupied fortress. Insignia, equipment, and trophies often commemorate the deeds on which that position rests.

The chieftain can plan and understands relationships within the group. The leader must convince warriors, important families, and other influential people that this leadership brings safety or success. A chieftain may act independently or owe an obligation to a more powerful ally. Goals often include protecting territory, securing resources for the group, recognition, and personal power. Aggressive behavior may arise from tradition, fear of losing authority, or a long-standing dispute with neighbors. Origins and appearance alone do not determine willingness to honor an agreement.

Once per battle, Battle Cry temporarily strengthens the attacks of up to two allies. Battle Fury increases the chieftain's melee attack when below half of maximum HP, so a wounded chieftain remains dangerous. The party can investigate the dispute's cause, negotiate over prisoners, or expose an outside manipulator. An offer must account for how the chieftain will explain it to the community. Removing a genuine threat to that community may produce a stronger agreement than a merely enforced truce.

strings.1× za souboj může před svým útokem zvoli: Once per battle, before attacking, may choose up to 2 allies; they gain +1 to their final ATTACK until the start of the chieftain's next turn. While below half of maximum HP, the chieftain gains +1 to its final melee ATTACK.

best/arcimag.name: Archmage
profile: An archmage is an exceptionally experienced magic user whose knowledge and influence exceed those of an ordinary wizard. An archmage may lead a school, serve as an adviser, manage a protected residence, or work in seclusion for many years. In Elaria, this work leaves behind pupils, research results, and interventions that have affected the wider region. A study, tower, or underground laboratory is a place where everyday life meets power most people do not understand.

An archmage is intelligent and accustomed to thinking several steps ahead. One may direct apprentices, servants, or a community of specialists, or instead avoid anyone who would restrict the work. Goals may include knowledge, protection, influence, or completing a particular project. Long experience provides perspective, but may also strengthen the belief that others cannot judge these decisions. Conflict may arise from a dangerous experiment, concealed consequences, or a goal for which the archmage is willing to sacrifice other people's safety.

Once per battle, Chain Lightning allows magical attacks against up to two targets. The Power Crystal supports defense against the first physical attack each round and strengthens the archmage's magic. Destroying or taking away the crystal removes this protection, reduces the spell bonus to +1 and magical protection to zero; the resulting magical attack is 14 and magical defense is 13. The party can prepare a way to disconnect the crystal safely or negotiate an end to a particular plan. The archmage's strength thus has a clear mechanical dependency that can be discovered and exploited, rather than making the encounter depend solely on trading attacks.

strings.1× za souboj může místo běžného útoku na: Once per battle, replace a normal attack with magical attacks against up to 2 targets (spell bonus +3); roll separately for each. With the crystal, gain +2 PDEF against the first physical attack each round. If the crystal is destroyed or taken, this ends; spell bonus drops +3 → +1 and magical protection +3 → 0 (MATK 14, MDEF 13).

hero/clovek-bojovnik.name: Human – Warrior
profile: A human warrior suits a player who wants to begin with a straightforward role and gradually find a personal style. The character might be a bridge guard, an experienced warrior's apprentice, or a villager who decided to protect others. The story rests on choices rather than exceptional ancestry: whom to help, what to learn, and when to favor negotiation over a drawn sword.

Within the party, the warrior helps keep danger away from more vulnerable allies and gives them room to make decisions. The character may guard a retreat, accompany a negotiator, or hold an important passage. The role is useful outside combat too: protecting travelers, preparing an expedition, and handling situations where someone needs support. Courage may mean admitting a mistake or choosing a safer route, rather than accepting every challenge.

The racial ability Adaptability allows a reroll after the character's own failed roll once per adventure. Vaelor creates a new random permutation, the player chooses a number again, and the better of the two results is used. The class adds Protect: once per battle, the warrior may take an attack directed at a nearby ally. The attack is resolved against the warrior's defense instead. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. The listed values form the basis of a level-one character; personality, name, relationships, and the reason for adventuring are decided during character creation.

hero/elf-bojovnik.name: Elf – Warrior
profile: An elf warrior combines attentiveness and a keen mind with a willingness to face danger directly. The character may protect a forest road, accompany a messenger, or leave home because of an unfulfilled promise. Within the party, the warrior serves as a defender who watches the surroundings and seeks a good position. A thoughtful approach can complement brute strength, but does not automatically grant an extra special strike.

Within the party, the warrior helps keep danger away from more vulnerable allies and gives them room to make decisions. The character may guard a retreat, accompany a negotiator, or hold an important passage. The role is useful outside combat too: protecting travelers, preparing an expedition, and handling situations where someone needs support. Courage may mean admitting a mistake or choosing a safer route, rather than accepting every challenge.

The racial ability Keen Sight automatically reveals a distant visible detail, tracks, or movement unless they are magically or objectively hidden. The class adds Protect: once per battle, the warrior may take an attack directed at a nearby ally. The attack is resolved against the warrior's defense instead. hero/trpaslik-bojovnik.name: Dwarf – Warrior
profile: A dwarf warrior is a dependable pillar of the party, especially where combat meets stone and underground spaces. The character may come from a mining settlement, serve as the guard of a mountain gate, or search for a missing relative. Strength provides a natural foundation for direct confrontation. Lower agility encourages planning the route, retreat, and position from which to protect the others.

Within the party, the warrior helps keep danger away from more vulnerable allies and gives them room to make decisions. The character may guard a retreat, accompany a negotiator, or hold an important passage. The role is useful outside combat too: protecting travelers, preparing an expedition, and handling situations where someone needs support. Courage may mean admitting a mistake or choosing a safer route, rather than accepting every challenge.

The racial ability Stone Sense automatically reveals cavities, secret passages, unstable rock, high-quality ore, or unusual properties of stone in a relevant stone or underground environment. The class adds Protect: once per battle, the warrior may take an attack directed at a nearby ally. The attack is resolved against the warrior's defense instead. hero/ork-bojovnik.name: Orc – Warrior
profile: An orc warrior excels in strength and the courage to face threats at close quarters. The character's past may involve defending a family, serving in a guard, or trying to put right a leader's mistake. Appearance does not determine personality: the warrior may be a patient protector, a cheerful companion, or someone still learning to control anger. Reliable allies matter as much to this character as to any other hero.

Within the party, the warrior helps keep danger away from more vulnerable allies and gives them room to make decisions. The character may guard a retreat, accompany a negotiator, or hold an important passage. The role is useful outside combat too: protecting travelers, preparing an expedition, and handling situations where someone needs support. Courage may mean admitting a mistake or choosing a safer route, rather than accepting every challenge.

The racial ability Battle Fury grants +1 to the result of every melee attack while the character is below half of maximum HP. The class adds Protect: once per battle, the warrior may take an attack directed at a nearby ally. The attack is resolved against the warrior's defense instead. hero/pulcik-bojovnik.name: Halfling – Warrior
profile: A halfling warrior shows that the decision to protect others does not depend on a character's size. The character may guard a home village, defend travelers, or set out in search of someone who once offered help. Low strength restricts some equipment, making it important to choose a weapon and shield according to their actual requirements. Courage may grow from caring about particular people, rather than a desire to defeat every larger opponent.

Within the party, the warrior helps keep danger away from more vulnerable allies and gives them room to make decisions. The character may guard a retreat, accompany a negotiator, or hold an important passage. The role is useful outside combat too: protecting travelers, preparing an expedition, and handling situations where someone needs support. Courage may mean admitting a mistake or choosing a safer route, rather than accepting every challenge.

hero/clovek-hranicar.name: Human – Ranger
profile: A human ranger guides others between the safety of settlements and landscapes absent even from local maps. The character may be a former shepherd, a guardian of trails, or a curious traveler. By noticing changes in the environment, the ranger helps the group decide which route to take. Adaptability supports a character who learns from mistakes and seeks solutions even when the original plan fails.

Within the party, the ranger helps plan routes, follow usable tracks, and recognize changes in the landscape. Before entering a dangerous place, the character can investigate approaches, cover, and ways back. Tracking does not reveal every creature's identity or intentions; the information needs to be combined with other clues. The ranger is therefore useful when rescuing a missing person, finding water, and deciding when the group should stop.

The racial ability Adaptability allows a reroll after the character's own failed roll once per adventure. Vaelor creates a new random permutation, the player chooses a number again, and the better of the two results is used. The class adds Tracker: automatically determine the direction in which a sought person or animal departed, provided usable tracks exist. Magic is a tool for understanding as well as protecting the group. An interesting story can grow around the reason for learning: a search for knowledge, a desire to help someone close, or an answer to an event from the past.

Within the party, the wizard helps recognize magic and select a known spell for the actual problem. The character contributes to exploring unusual places, solving puzzles, and protecting allies. Magic Sense reveals the presence of magic but does not automatically identify its purpose, trigger, or safety. Careful questions are therefore part of the wizard's work.

hero/clovek-zlodej.name: Human – Rogue
profile: A human rogue specializes in moving discreetly and reaching places ordinary routes do not lead to. The character may explore ruins, assist the guard, or be a former pickpocket who changed course. The class name does not determine the character's morality. Adaptability supports a hero who improvises and learns from failure, while real values emerge through whom the character helps and what the character refuses to do.

Within the party, the rogue helps gather information, pass unnoticed, and gain access using suitable tools. The greatest contribution often comes before combat, when scouting helps the group understand what it can avoid. Soft Steps makes ordinary sneaking easier, but an exceptional obstacle may require a roll and the ability cannot create cover where none exists. hero/pulcik-lecitel.name: Halfling – Healer
profile: A halfling healer is an attentive helper who often gets to know people closely and notices the group's everyday needs. The character may grow up in a small village, accompany a caravan, or search for a missing teacher. Low strength increases the importance of light equipment and cooperation. Luck offers one exceptional rescue from failure, but the most reliable help still comes from preparation, knowledge, and the willingness to ask others for support in time.

Within the party, the healer helps decide when to treat injuries, use a known healing spell, and secure safe rest. First Aid is a separate ability and does not consume the magical healing limit. The HP restored depends on actual Intelligence and cannot exceed the patient's maximum. A good healer needs room to work and support from others; preventing danger is often as valuable as another use of healing magic.

The racial ability Lucky Break turns the character's own failed virtual roll into a narrow success once per adventure. The roll is not repeated; this is the minimum success required, with no additional advantage. The adventure brings a personal reason to listen even to people others overlook. The role suits a player who enjoys speaking in character, but can also be a quieter observer whose well-chosen words encourage the group at the right moment.

Within the party, the bard helps with negotiations, learning local stories, and supporting allies. hero/vila-hranicar.name: Fairy – Ranger
profile: A fairy ranger may explore overgrown trails, help lost travelers, and investigate changes in places close to the community. Agility supports exploration, while low strength limits heavier protection and equipment. This combination suits a character who seeks connections in nature and helps the whole group travel safely. Personal curiosity can lead to an expedition just as readily as the duty to protect a home.

Within the party, the ranger helps plan routes, follow usable tracks, and recognize changes in the landscape. Before entering a dangerous place, the character can investigate approaches, cover, and ways back. Tracking does not reveal every creature's identity or intentions; the information needs to be combined with other clues. The ranger is therefore useful when rescuing a missing person, finding water, and deciding when the group should stop.

The racial ability Fairy Dust makes every healing performed by the fairy restore one extra HP. The class adds Tracker: automatically determine the direction in which a sought person or animal departed, provided usable tracks exist. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. hero/vila-kouzelnik.name: Fairy – Wizard
profile: A fairy wizard combines magical aptitude with high Intelligence and agility. The character may study with an experienced teacher, seek an explanation for a strange phenomenon, or learn spells useful for protecting a home. Low strength and fewer HP encourage cautious positioning within the party. Fairy Dust takes effect during healing, but does not remove the need to genuinely know a healing spell and use it correctly.

Within the party, the wizard helps recognize magic and select a known spell for the actual problem. The character contributes to exploring unusual places, solving puzzles, and protecting allies. Meeting the required Intelligence alone does not teach a new spell; that knowledge must come from a teacher, a book, or the story. Magic Sense reveals the presence of magic but does not automatically identify its purpose, trigger, or safety. Careful questions are therefore part of the wizard's work.

The racial ability Fairy Dust makes every healing performed by the fairy restore one extra HP. The class adds Magic Sense: automatically recognize that an object, place, or being is magical. This alone does not reveal the magic's exact type, purpose, trigger, or danger. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. The listed values form the basis of a level-one character; personality, name, relationships, and the reason for adventuring are decided during character creation.

hero/vila-zlodej.name: Fairy – Rogue
profile: A fairy rogue may be a scout, a carrier of secret messages, or a finder of stolen objects. Agility and discreet movement provide a clear role in exploration, while low strength limits solutions based on force. The character need not be selfish or dishonest. Soft Steps does not allow disappearing in open ground, and a fairy's appearance does not itself replace cover, so carefully reading the actual environment is essential.

Within the party, the rogue helps gather information, pass unnoticed, and gain access using suitable tools. The greatest contribution often comes before combat, when scouting helps the group understand what it can avoid. Soft Steps makes ordinary sneaking easier, but an exceptional obstacle may require a roll and the ability cannot create cover where none exists. Others' trust depends on the rogue's decisions, so defining personal boundaries and an attitude toward other people's property is useful.

The racial ability Fairy Dust makes every healing performed by the fairy restore one extra HP. The class adds Soft Steps: Vaelor assumes success during ordinary sneaking. Only an exceptional obstacle requires a roll; the ability does not allow hiding where it is objectively impossible. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. The listed values form the basis of a level-one character; personality, name, relationships, and the reason for adventuring are decided during character creation.

hero/vila-lecitel.name: Fairy – Healer
profile: A fairy healer is a natural choice for a player who wants to protect others through care and magic. The character may look after a forest community, accompany friends, or seek help for an ill loved one. Fairy Dust supports healing, and high Intelligence strengthens the main role. The healer is small and vulnerable, however, making cooperation important: the party protects the healer just as the healer helps the party.

Within the party, the healer helps decide when to treat injuries, use a known healing spell, and secure safe rest. First Aid is a separate ability and does not consume the magical healing limit. The HP restored depends on actual Intelligence and cannot exceed the patient's maximum. A good healer needs room to work and support from others; preventing danger is often as valuable as another use of healing magic.

The racial ability Fairy Dust makes every healing performed by the fairy restore one extra HP. The class adds First Aid: once per battle, restore ⌈INT/2⌉ HP to yourself or one ally, up to their maximum. This is not a healing spell and does not consume the magical healing limit. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. The listed values form the basis of a level-one character; personality, name, relationships, and the reason for adventuring are decided during character creation.

hero/vila-bard.name: Fairy – Bard
profile: A fairy bard may bring songs from remote places, connect different communities, and encourage friends on a demanding journey. Agility and luck support this style, but the relationship with listeners remains decisive. The character may be cheerful, calm, or shy. Music need not be the focus of every scene; a well-chosen story or a small gesture can express support just as naturally.

Within the party, the bard helps with negotiations, learning local stories, and supporting allies. The character may mediate between people who misunderstand each other or recall an important connection at just the right time. Inspiration raises the bonus of a revealed virtual roll by one step, up to that category's maximum; it is not an unrestricted increase to every result. Storytelling, music, and listening also give the bard a meaningful role in scenes that do not lead to combat.

The racial ability Fairy Dust makes every healing performed by the fairy restore one extra HP. The class adds Inspiration: once in a given battle or significant scene, after a virtual roll is revealed, raise your own or an ally's roll bonus by one step, up to that category's maximum. It does not require a main action and cannot be used on an enemy. Choose starting equipment according to the requirements this particular hero meets. The listed values form the basis of a level-one character; personality, name, relationships, and the reason for adventuring are decided during character creation.

equip/dyka.name: Dagger
profile: A dagger is a small weapon carried in Elaria by scouts, travelers, and people who do not want to burden themselves with large weapons. Its value lies in its light weight and easy storage. It may be an ordinary work knife adapted for defense or a personal possession bearing a family emblem. Its appearance and origins can tell the owner's story without changing its game values.

It suits a character who relies on agility and can serve as a backup when the main weapon is unavailable. Being easy to conceal does not make it automatically invisible during a search. In the story, it can help with ordinary tasks when the situation allows, but does not replace every specialist tool. A lost dagger bearing a recognizable emblem may provide a clue to its owner.

Attacks use Agility (AGI). The 1H designation means it uses one hand. The minimum is AGI4, and its catalog physical attack bonus (PATK) is +1. The price is 6 sp. A hero's total attack is then calculated from attributes and the applicable rules; the listed weapon bonus is not the entire final attack.

equip/bojova-hul.name: Quarterstaff
profile: A quarterstaff is a simple, long weapon that may be carried by a pilgrim, a trail warden, or a martial teacher's student. It may look like an ordinary walking aid, yet its origins need not be humble. Carefully worked wood, a repaired section, and a carved mark may reveal who made it and why its owner keeps it.

In combat, it relies on agility and requires both hands. Choosing a staff therefore depends on whether the hero also needs to hold a shield or another object. It offers an inexpensive, straightforward option for a first expedition. Judge its use as a support or to test an ordinary obstacle according to the circumstances; the staff itself grants no extra bonus to climbing or finding traps.

Attacks use Agility (AGI). The 2H designation means it uses both hands. The minimum is AGI4, and its catalog physical attack bonus (PATK) is +1. The price is 3 sp. equip/kyj.name: Club
profile: A club is a simple weapon relying on strength, found in the hands of a village guard, in a camp, or among travelers with modest equipment. It needs neither an ornate blade nor a prestigious family history to serve its basic purpose. Its workmanship and wear can distinguish an improvised weapon from one its owner has used regularly for years.

It suits a hero with limited funds who already meets the strength requirement. Leaving one hand free allows suitable additional equipment. The club's simplicity does not guarantee an advantage against armor or a special stunning effect. Consider your whole style of play when choosing: one hero may prefer an inexpensive starting weapon, while another pays more for a more effective weapon suited to their attributes.

Attacks use Strength (STR). The 1H designation means it uses one hand. The minimum is STR4, and its catalog physical attack bonus (PATK) is +1. The price is 1 sp. profile: A short sword is an agility-based weapon suited to an adventurer who wants a straightforward start without relying entirely on strength. In Elaria, it may come from a city workshop or an armory, or be a reward for a first service. Its ornamentation can show its owner's connection to the place or people who entrusted it to them.

It uses one hand, leaving room for other suitable equipment. It often fits the lighter equipment of a scout or bard, provided the hero meets its requirements. Its smaller size grants no automatic bonus to speed or stealth. In the story, the sword may embody a promise, mark a period of service, or form part of a mystery involving an abandoned guard post.

equip/kopi.name: Spear
profile: A spear is a one-handed, strength-based weapon used in Elaria by road guards, settlement defenders, and people accustomed to open country. Its long shaft and point give it a distinctive appearance. Different groups may mark their spears with colors or emblems, so finding one in the wilderness can help identify an expedition's origins.

The catalog explicitly allows the spear to be used as a thrown weapon as well. This offers a way to change your approach to suit the situation, although after throwing it you are naturally no longer holding it. Its length alone grants neither an extra attack nor an automatic way to stop an opponent. When choosing it, consider the surroundings and how the hero will retrieve the weapon after a throw.

equip/rapir.name: Rapier
profile: A rapier is an agility-based alternative to a sword for a hero who favors a precise, thoughtful fighting style. In Elaria, it may belong to a fencer, a city defender, or a traveler following a personal tradition. An ornate hilt may bear the emblem of a school or family, or simply recall a reward for a task well done.

Its higher agility requirement reflects its place among more effective weapons. It uses one hand, so choose it with the character's role and other equipment in mind. It has no automatic ability to pierce armor or disarm an opponent. A story might involve finding a teacher, recovering a lost rapier, or settling a dispute over who truly owns an important possession.

equip/hak-s-lanem.name: Grappling hook and rope
profile: A grappling hook and rope is a tool for situations where a connection can be secured to a place the hero cannot reach directly. In Elaria, it may belong to a scout, a mountain dweller, or a group rescuing people from difficult places. The hook and rope's design may point to a local workshop or an expedition from which only the equipment remains.

The bonus when climbing or overcoming an obstacle applies only if the hook can be secured safely. The player must describe a suitable anchor point and approach, rather than having the item automatically open any route. The catalog grants neither a combat attack nor unconditional success. The party can work together to find the right approach and decide who will help the others.

Rules effect: +2 AGI when climbing or overcoming an obstacle, if the hook can be secured safely. The price is 8 sp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/dalekohled.name: Spyglass
profile: A spyglass helps examine visible distant places and may be a valuable gift for a scout in Elaria. It may belong to a tower guard, captain, traveler, or scholar observing the landscape. Its case and markings may identify the maker or a former owner. Obtaining a clear observation often changes an entire expedition's decision.

It supports a test for searching for or identifying something at a great distance. It does not allow sight through a wall, reveal an invisible creature, or automatically explain an observed person's intentions. From a safe vantage point, the party can investigate approaches, movement, or changes along a route. The information must be combined with other knowledge; a distant detail can be important while still being incomplete.

Rules effect: +2 INT when searching for or identifying something at a great distance. The price is 3 gp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/obvazy.name: Bandages
profile: Bandages are consumable supplies for ordinary treatment and a reminder that care can begin with practical equipment. In Elaria, they may come from a healer's workshop, a garrison's supplies, or a grateful settlement's gift. Their role in the story may be small yet important: someone made sure the party did not set out entirely unprepared.

They provide a bonus to one ordinary treatment test. They are not automatically a spell, do not directly restore a particular number of hit points, and do not replace every option available to a healer. The party can decide whom to use them for and where to replenish supplies. Missing bandages may lead to a small mission to deliver help or an encounter with someone offering both knowledge and equipment.

Rules effect: +1 INT to one ordinary test to treat an injury. The price is 3 sp. This is a consumable supply; account for its consumption when used. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/prazdna-lahvicka.name: Empty vial
profile: An empty vial is an ordinary container for a small amount of liquid. In Elaria, it may be carried by a researcher, healer, craftsperson, or curious adventurer. A mark on the glass, its shape, and a small inscription can identify its origins without giving the item itself a magical ability. Sometimes an empty container is a reminder of what it once held.

It is useful for keeping an ordinary liquid and clearly describing a discovery. It does not automatically turn its contents into a potion or guarantee their safety or the preservation of a magical effect. The party may want to take a sample for someone who understands it. Identifying the contents and using them are separate questions that must follow from the story and the rules.

Rules effect: Holding a small amount of ordinary liquid. The price is 5 cp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/pergamen.name: Parchment
profile: Parchment is a consumable writing material used to record a message, note, or map. In Elaria, it may come from an ordinary workshop, a scholar's supplies, or a messenger's luggage. Its value can change with its contents: a blank sheet is a supply, while a written sheet may be the only record of an important event.

It helps share information and preserve things the party does not want to rely on memory alone to remember. It does not create an accurate map or a magical scroll by itself. Writing requires suitable tools and information. Finding part of a message may begin a search for its author, recipient, or missing continuation; judge the contents by clues rather than the sheet's appearance alone.

Rules effect: Writing messages, notes, or maps. The price is 2 cp. This is a consumable supply; account for its consumption when used. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/brk.name: Quill
profile: A quill is an ordinary writing tool for a hero who wants to record notes and messages. In Elaria, it may accompany a scholar, storyteller, merchant, or curious scout. It may be simple or kept in a personal case. This small item can easily connect the expedition's practical side with a memory of someone who taught the character to write.

A quill needs other writing supplies and a suitable surface; it does not provide an unlimited supply of text by itself. It grants no automatic Intelligence bonus and creates no magical writings. The party may use it to draw a map, write a message to the guard, or list their discoveries. Distinctive handwriting or a missing writing tool can contribute to a story centered on information.

Rules effect: Writing tool. The price is 1 cp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

Its color and container may express a tradition or origin. Appearance alone, however, does not mean magical contents or guarantee that a written message will seem trustworthy to its reader.

It is used with a suitable writing tool and surface. The party can record discoveries, draw a simple map, or prepare a message for an absent ally. The catalog grants ink no automatic ability to create magical scrolls, invisible writing, or someone else's signature. The story may involve a missing supply or a workshop's mark on a found vial.

Rules effect: Supply for ordinary writing. The price is 5 cp. This is a consumable supply; account for its consumption when used. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/mech-s-vinem.name: Wine skin
profile: A wine skin is a traveling supply that may be intended in Elaria for a feast, trade, or delivery to an adult resident of a settlement. Its markings may identify its origin, and its contents may become part of a small agreement. In the game, it is important to preserve its precise, limited effect and not treat an ordinary supply as a healing potion.

The catalog explicitly states that it does not restore hit points. In gameplay, it may dull ordinary pain during treatment only when pain is the sole obstacle to calmly carrying out the procedure. It removes neither poison, a curse, nor the injury itself. The party may deliver or trade the supply, or use it in a social arrangement according to the story; it grants no automatic additional healing bonuses.

Rules effect: Does not restore HP. May dull ordinary pain during treatment if pain is the only obstacle to calmly carrying out the procedure. The price is 3 sp. This is a consumable supply; account for its consumption when used. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. equip/loutna.name: Lute
profile: A lute belongs to evenings around a campfire, songs of past expeditions, and performances where a bard first makes a name for themselves. Its strings can accompany a voice, conversation, or dance. Its carved body and worn case tell of its owner's travels, but a precious appearance alone grants no additional rules advantage.

It suits the story of a traveling musician who builds relationships through songs and remembers local ballads. A performance may open a conversation with an innkeeper or attract listeners, but their reactions depend on the circumstances. The instrument does not control its audience's decisions or guarantee success in negotiation by itself. It needs protection against damage while traveling.

Rules effect: +1 CHA during a musical performance. The price is 2 gp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/mandolina.name: Mandolin
profile: A mandolin offers a bright, lively sound suited to dance tunes and energetic accompaniment. In Elaria, it may be carried by a wandering player, a member of a small band, or a hero who learned music at home. The musician determines the performance's personal style: the same instrument may accompany a cheerful celebration or a quiet remembrance of a lost friend.

It is useful when a character wants to reach people through a musical performance and take part in local life. Knowing a favorite tune can begin an encounter, rather than automatically persuading every listener. equip/harfa.name: Harp
profile: A harp combines the gentle sound of strings with a striking silhouette that can grace a hall or a modest performance. Its owner need not be a court musician: they may preserve family songs or travel in search of forgotten melodies. Its size, material, and decoration can be adapted to the character while its game values remain as listed in the catalog.

It suits musical scenes intended to create a mood and encourage an audience to listen. Music may accompany a celebration, farewell, or the telling of a legend, but does not by itself replace a sleep or healing spell. On an expedition, it makes sense to agree on safe transport. A broken string or a lost composition can naturally begin a small adventure.

Rules effect: +1 CHA during a musical performance. The price is 2 gp. The item is reusable rather than a single-use supply. Its listed effect applies to the situation it is intended for. Additional bonuses, other forms of protection, and new magical abilities are not part of this entry.

equip/dudy.name: Bagpipes
profile: Bagpipes have a distinctive, penetrating sound suited to communal dancing, processions, and outdoor celebrations. In the story, they may recall a mountain traveler's home or a village tradition that brings everyone together at harvest time. Their owner determines the repertoire and mood; the instrument itself grants neither battle commands nor magical influence.

A bagpipe performance can attract attention and give the party an opportunity to introduce themselves to local people. Its distinctive sound also makes it unsuitable for quiet scouting, so the place and the player's intention matter. The audience's response is not guaranteed in advance. A forgotten festive tune or a competition between musicians can offer a more interesting scene than simply rolling for success.

equip/maly-buben.name: Small drum
profile: A small drum carries a rhythm that can accompany a song, dance, or march. Its simple appearance does not mean a simple performance: a skilled player can work with tempo, silence, and the audience's expectations. In Elaria, it may belong to a street performer, traveling storyteller, or member of a festive procession without needing a special magical origin.

It fits group music and scenes where the party contributes to a celebration or earns a chance to share its own story. A rhythm can serve as an agreed signal if it can be heard, but the catalog grants it no separate combat bonus. When deciding to use it, the heroes' willingness to attract attention also matters.

equip/pistalka.name: Whistle
profile: A whistle is a small instrument that fits into traveling equipment and may accompany a hero from childhood games to adventures. A simple tune can easily become associated with a memory, region, or person. In the story, it may be an ordinary craftsperson's product or a farewell gift; its effect does not depend on rarity or an elaborate appearance.

It is useful for small musical performances, rest, and playing together. It can also produce an agreed sound signal, but neither the range nor reliability of that use is automatically unlimited. Its unusual catalog feature is the connection to Luck, which must be distinguished from the Charisma used by other instruments. The whistle therefore does not improve every social interaction or every chance event.

profile: A minor healing potion is a modest supply of help for a hero returning from a dangerous trail or continuing after an injury. The vial may come from a healer's workshop, a market, or a grateful person. Its color and scent can vary with its maker's story; appearance alone grants no new effects or greater healing power.

It makes sense as a small reserve when the party does not want to use a more valuable resource immediately. Deciding whom to give it to can reveal the characters' priorities and relationships. Restoring hit points does not automatically remove poisoning, illness, or a curse. When planning supplies, distinguish an ordinary injury from a problem that needs another specific solution.

equip/lecivy-lektvar.name: Healing potion
profile: A healing potion is the kind of equipment whose value a hero understands when a companion needs help. It may be the work of a local healer or a carefully kept gift. Its recipe in the story, stopper, and maker's mark can give the vial individuality without changing the exact amount of hit points restored as listed in the catalog.

It offers the party a reserve for continuing an expedition after an injury. It is worth thinking about before entering a dangerous area and agreeing on who will carry it. Healing does not itself resolve every cause of danger: poison, a curse, or a hostile environment may remain active. Deciding whether to use a supply now or save it for later is a natural part of an adventure.

profile: A greater healing potion is a more substantial healing supply that the party may guard for a particularly difficult moment. In the story, it may come from a respected healer or form part of a reward for demanding service. Its designation refers to restoring hit points, rather than an unlimited ability to repair any harm to the body, magic, or fate.

It is useful as an important reserve for an injured expedition member. Its greater effect does not mean it should be used without thought for every minor injury; its value depends on the current situation and other available options. It grants no automatic invulnerability for the rest of a battle. After using it, the party must still deal with the enemy, a safe retreat, and the source of danger.

In the story, it may come from an herbalist, alchemist, or experienced traveler familiar with the dangers of their region. Its value lies in its specific effect; a rare label or mysterious name alone does not make it universal protection.

The party may prepare it before traveling to places where poisoned food, toxic substances, or other ordinary sources of poisoning are a danger. It helps resolve existing ordinary poisoning, but the catalog grants neither preventive immunity nor automatic removal of a magical curse. When the condition's nature is unclear, first establish what the character is actually facing.

The party may save it for a demanding encounter or a scene involving a physical obstacle. Its recipe in the story may seem rough or refined, but its effect remains the same: it increases Strength for the limited duration listed in the rules.

It helps with planning a crucial moment of an expedition, but does not replace a sensible approach, suitable equipment, or cooperation with others. Increased Strength does not promise success on every attempt and grants no further unlisted abilities. It therefore makes sense to time its use for a specific significant scene or battle; it does not permanently change the original character.

equip/plast-sucha.name: Cloak of Dryness
profile: The Cloak of Dryness is appreciated by anyone who spends time traveling and does not want to search for dry clothes after ordinary rain. It may seem like a practical gift from an experienced pilgrim who knows how easily dampness complicates an expedition. Its magic is convenient and specific; it is not unlimited protection against water or every effect of the weather.

It protects the wearer and items sheltered beneath the cloak from being soaked by ordinary rain. Items stored outside its coverage cannot automatically be considered protected. When fording a river or entering the water, it does not replace other necessary equipment. It suits long journeys, protecting traveling supplies, and stories where small practical advantages truly matter.

It uses the "Cloak" slot and the base item is a "cloak". Ordinary rain does not soak the wearer or items sheltered beneath it. The item has no other explicitly listed requirement. Its catalog value is 10 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

equip/plast-stinu.name: Cloak of Shadows
profile: The Cloak of Shadows is intended for a character who needs an advantage when hiding. Its appearance may be plain enough to resemble ordinary traveling clothes at first glance. In the story, it may come from a scout's equipment or a commission for a cautious messenger. Its name means neither complete invisibility nor the right to pass any patrol unnoticed.

It helps with an attempt to hide, but the outcome still depends on the circumstances and the relevant rules. The hero needs to find a suitable place, consider the light, and avoid drawing attention through unsuitable actions. The bonus does not extend to every dexterous task or all attacks. An escape that combines the cloak's advantage with a good plan can create an interesting scene.

It uses the "Cloak" slot and the base item is a "cloak". The listed bonus is +1 AGI when hiding. It applies only to an attempt to hide. The item has no other explicitly listed requirement. Its catalog value is 16 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

equip/roba-ohne.name: Robe of Flame
profile: The Robe of Flame is clothing focused on casting spells from the Fire school. In the story, it may bear the marks of a teacher, a circle of mages, or a personal tradition of study. Its appearance may emphasize the wearer's determination and power, but the fabric's color does not determine its actual effect. The rules grant it an increase to the magical attack of this specific school.

It suits a character who can actually cast Fire spells and wants to support that part of their equipment. It does not teach anyone new spells or fulfill their other requirements. The robe's name also promises no fire resistance. When choosing equipment, distinguish strengthening your own Fire spells from protection against flames and other attacks.

It uses the "Body" slot and the base item is a "robe". The listed bonus is +1 Fire MATK. It adds a direct +1 MATK when casting a spell from the Fire school. Requirement: Ability to cast Fire spells. Its catalog value is 20 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

equip/kozena-zbroj-poutnika.name: Pilgrim's Leather Armor
profile: Pilgrim's Leather Armor is based on ordinary leather armor and adds a magical increase to its protection. It may accompany a traveler who values flexible equipment and frequently stays beyond the safety of cities. Old repairs and signs of travel can provide details for the story without changing the defense value listed in the rules.

It is useful for a hero who meets the strength requirement. Preserve the calculation order: first the leather armor's base value and its coefficient, then the additional bonus. The appearance of light traveling equipment does not mean automatic protection against weather, poison, or magic. In the story, its known origins may be more valuable than its ornamentation, particularly if a missing guide once wore it.

It uses the "Body" slot and the base item is "leather armor". The listed bonus is an additional +1 PDEF. Apply the coefficient to the leather armor's base value, then add +1 PDEF. Requirement: STR4. Its catalog value is 25 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

equip/rukavice-prilnavosti.name: Gloves of Grip
profile: The Gloves of Grip are a magical aid for climbing and may be valuable to a scout moving among cliffs and high walls. In the story, they may have been left by an experienced climber or a master who wanted to make work easier for apprentices. Their practical effect relates to climbing rather than every activity performed with the hands.

It makes sense to use them with a planned route and appropriate safety measures. An Agility bonus when climbing does not guarantee that the character can overcome any surface or survive a fall. They do not automatically grant the ability to walk on ceilings. Their advantage may be important in a tense scene, but the terrain, difficulty, and party's decisions still matter.

It uses the "Hands" slot and the base item is "gloves". The listed bonus is +1 AGI when climbing. The item has no other explicitly listed requirement. Its catalog value is 12 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

equip/prsten-tepla.name: Ring of Warmth
profile: The Ring of Warmth offers a traveler protection against ordinary natural cold. It may be an unobtrusive part of a mountain guide's equipment or a gift from someone concerned for a hero's safety on a winter journey. Its value is chiefly practical. A plain appearance does not change its effect, and its name must not be mistaken for complete resistance to all icy dangers.

It helps in ordinary cold weather, but extreme and magical cold affect the wearer normally under the catalog's rules. It therefore remains important to distinguish discomfort while traveling from genuinely dangerous conditions. It provides neither protection for the whole party nor automatic survival of an icy attack. In the story, it may be a treasured small item a hero lends to a friend without gaining further new abilities.

profile: The Sword of Precision is based on a one-handed sword and adds a magical bonus to its physical attack. In the story, it may be the work of a meticulous master or a reward for service to someone who valued disciplined combat. Its name may recall a special reputation, but does not promise an automatic hit on every attack attempt.

The wielder must meet the same requirements as for an ordinary one-handed sword. The correct calculation order matters: apply the coefficient to the weapon's base value, then add the magical bonus. Do not add it to the base value first and multiply them together. The sword also grants no separate disarming ability or infallible way to find a weak point.

equip/hul-prirody.name: Staff of Nature
profile: The Staff of Nature combines a quarterstaff's base with support for Nature Magic's magical attack. Its origins in the story may involve a forest teacher, protecting an old grove, or a journey to learn about the landscape. Its material and ornamentation can express the wearer's relationship with nature. They do not, however, automatically grant the ability to speak with animals or command trees.

It is intended for a character who meets the required Agility and can cast Nature Magic. Physical attack still comes from the quarterstaff and its coefficient; the magical increase for this school is added directly. These two components must be distinguished. The staff does not strengthen spells from every school or teach its wielder a spell they do not yet know.

It uses the "Main + Off hand" slots and the base item is a "quarterstaff". The listed bonus is +1 Nature Magic MATK. Apply the Weapon coefficient to the staff's physical base value; add +1 MATK directly. Requirement: AGI4 + ability to cast Nature Magic. Its catalog value is 22 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

Its pockets and markings in the story can reflect the wearer's work, but its magical effect is specific: it increases the total result of one healing spell cast by the listed amount of hit points.

They may suit a scout, a cautious messenger, or a hero trying to escape unwanted attention. Their name grants no ability to fly, and the catalog does not promise the complete disappearance of every sign of the wearer's presence.

The advantage concerns ordinary visible tracks rather than absolute protection against every tracker. Deliberate tracking and unusual terrain may reveal movement. The character may also leave other evidence through their actions, noise, or a lost possession. In the story, the boots therefore help a good escape plan without replacing thought about what is actually happening behind the party.

It uses the "Feet" slot and the base item is "boots". Ordinary movement leaves no easily visible tracks; deliberate tracking or unusual terrain may reveal them. The item has no other explicitly listed requirement. Its catalog value is 14 gp. Follow the calculation and conditions of the bonus exactly; its origins in the story alone grant no additional abilities.

magic/obecna/svetelko.name: Wisp
profile: Wisp is a small, practical spell for dark corridors, evening reading, and moments when the party would rather not look for another torch. Its harmless glow can illuminate an object or a chosen point. It suits a wizard who uses magic for ordinary help and comfort as well as dangerous encounters.

During exploration, it makes the surroundings easier to see, but does not itself identify a trap or hidden opponent. The caster must also consider whether the light will reveal the party's presence. It can be turned off at any time, which helps when plans change. Its limited range and single active light source must also be respected when illuminating a larger space.

Exact effect: Creates harmless light with a range of about 5 m. The caster can turn it off at any time. Target: a point or object within reach. Duration: 1 hour. Restrictions: at most 1 active. Use requires at least Intelligence 5, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/zapaleni.name: Ignite
profile: Ignite turns a prepared candle, torch, or dry tinder into a small source of fire. It is a spell for readiness on the road: preparing the material properly matters as much as casting the spell itself. In a story, it can show the experience of a hero who first finds a suitable place and fuel, then turns to magic.

It is useful for lighting a prepared torch or starting a small fire where conditions permit. It is not intended to attack a creature and cannot target a carried item. The caster's wish alone will not overcome wet fuel. Once an ordinary fire has started, it must still be handled with care appropriate to the surroundings and the situation.

Exact effect: Ignites a small, prepared source of fire. Deals no damage and cannot ignite wet material. Target: a candle, torch, or dry tinder within sight. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: cannot target a creature or a carried item. Using it requires at least Intelligence 5, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/kouzelny-zvuk.name: Magic Sound
profile: Magic Sound creates a short, simple sound nearby. It might resemble a knock, a chime, or another basic signal, making it useful to a wizard who works with the attention of those around them. Its strength lies in an inventive idea and good timing. The spell cannot create a lengthy performance or a convincing conversation in a particular person's voice.

The party can use it as a brief signal or an attempt to distract someone, but a listener's reaction is not guaranteed. A suspicious guard may interpret the sound differently from a curious animal. Choosing a point within range and accounting for the short duration are essential; this spell cannot imitate the intelligible speech of a specific person.

Exact effect: Creates a simple sound lasting no more than 6 seconds. Cannot imitate the intelligible speech of a specific person. Target: a point within 10 m. Duration: at most 1 round. Restrictions: at most 1 active. Using it requires at least Intelligence 5, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/kouzelna-cistota.name: Magical Cleaning
profile: Magical Cleaning deals with the everyday dirt and unpleasant smells that accompany an expedition as faithfully as adventure itself. It cleans a small item or area without damaging it. In a story, it can prepare a hero for a meeting with someone important or reveal details on a surface previously hidden by mud and dust.

A clean appearance does not guarantee safety. A cleaned container may still contain poison, and a damaged item remains damaged. The spell is a practical aid to maintenance, rather than a general cure or a means of removing curses. During an investigation, it is also worth considering whether the dirt itself holds a clue that premature cleaning would erase.

Exact effect: Removes ordinary dirt, mud, dust, or odors without damaging the item. Target: an item or an area of up to 1 m². Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: does not remove poison, curses, or damage. Using it requires at least Intelligence 5, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/hledani-vody.name: Find Water
profile: Find Water points a traveler toward the nearest reachable source within a limited area. In dry country, it can provide a crucial reason to change course and serves as a reminder that a successful expedition also depends on everyday supplies. The spell does not conjure water into a waterskin or choose the most comfortable campsite for the whole party.

After learning the direction, the party must still reach the location and assess the source it finds. The water may not be safe to drink, and obstacles may await along the way. The information helps plan exploration and replenish supplies. The limit of one use per scene encourages thoughtful timing rather than aimless repeated attempts.

Exact effect: Shows the direction of the nearest reachable water source within 1 km. Does not determine whether the water is safe to drink. Target: caster. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: once per scene. Using it requires at least Intelligence 6, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/magicka-ruka.name: Magic Hand
profile: Magic Hand creates a visible aid for simple tasks involving a light, unattached item. It can lift something, bring it closer, or press a simple mechanism, making it useful for cautious handling from a short distance. Its capabilities are narrowly defined: it is not a universal force that can move any object or replace a skilled craftsperson.

The party can use its reach where it would rather not put its own hands immediately. However, the item's weight, its distance, and the simplicity of the task must be checked. The spell cannot attack, affect a creature, or perform complex fine work. It requires concentration, and its limited duration is a reason to prepare a plan before casting rather than during it.

Exact effect: Creates a visible magical hand that can lift, carry, or set down an item, or press a simple mechanism. This is not Telekinesis and cannot affect a creature. Target: an unattached item up to 2 kg within 5 m. Duration: concentration, at most 3 rounds. Restrictions: 1 hand; no attacks or complex fine work. Using it requires at least Intelligence 6, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/oprava-drobnosti.name: Minor Repair
profile: Minor Repair can mend simple damage to a nonmagical item, provided all of its parts are available. It is a spell that can save a broken strap or a small broken component far from a workshop. In a story, it rewards a hero who maintains their belongings instead of discarding them at the first sign of trouble.

First, determine what is actually broken and gather any missing parts. The spell does not restore consumed contents or lost magic, and repeated use on the same damage is limited. A practical repair may allow the journey to continue, but major reconstruction or the restoration of a destroyed item must be handled using other available means.

Exact effect: Mends a crack, a broken strap, or a small broken component. Does not restore consumed contents or magic. Target: 1 nonmagical item no larger than a backpack. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: once per instance of damage; all parts must be present. Using it requires at least Intelligence 6, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/odhaleni-magie.name: Detect Magic
profile: Detect Magic helps determine whether a chosen item, creature, or nearby area carries a magical influence and identifies the closest school. It is useful for an initial examination of an unfamiliar find. It provides a clue for further investigation, rather than a complete guide to safely using everything the party discovers in an old chest or forgotten shrine.

Casting may be followed by a conversation with an expert, a study of markings, or careful observation. The spell does not reveal the exact effect, its trigger, or how to dispel it. Discovered magic may therefore remain both a mystery and a danger. Its limited range and use per scene must be considered when deciding which find to examine first.

Exact effect: Detects the presence of magic and its closest school. Does not reveal its exact effect, trigger, or how to dispel it. Target: 1 item, creature, or area within 5 m. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: once per scene. Using it requires at least Intelligence 7, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/kouzelny-klic.name: Magic Key
profile: Magic Key attempts to open an ordinary nonmagical lock using the caster's Intelligence. It can offer an alternative in a story where the party lacks the right key or a skilled locksmith. However, it is not a universal command for every door to open: the quality of the particular lock and success on the required check both matter.

Before casting, it is worth examining the door and its surroundings. Successfully unlocking it does not remove a possible trap, and the spell cannot overcome a magical lock. There is only one attempt per lock, so the party also needs a backup plan. A locked route may still call for negotiation, a search for the original key, or another suitable approach.

Exact effect: Makes an INT check against 7/9/11 depending on the lock's quality. Success opens the lock; it does not dispel a magical lock or disarm a trap. Target: 1 ordinary nonmagical lock within reach. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: 1 attempt per lock. Using it requires at least Intelligence 7, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/obecna/drobny-magicky-stit.name: Minor Magic Shield
profile: Minor Magic Shield offers brief protection to the caster or an ally they can see. It suits a moment when the party expects an imminent attack and wants to support a threatened member. Its effect is small but specific; it does not guarantee complete safety or create a lasting layer of defense for the entire adventure.

Timing matters, because the protection ends after the next attack against the target or after a short time. Casting makes sense alongside a clear plan for who needs protection right now. The bonuses do not stack with another magical bonus to the same defense, so existing effects must be considered rather than automatically layering them.

Exact effect: The target gains +1 to both PDEF and MDEF against the next attack. Target: caster or 1 ally within sight. Duration: until the next attack against the target, at most 1 round. Restrictions: twice per combat; does not stack with another magical bonus to the same defense. Using it requires at least Intelligence 7, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/ohen/jiskra.name: Spark
profile: Spark is a basic offensive spell of the Fire school, aimed at a single visible target. It may be the caster's first striking display of combat magic: a brief moment when concentration becomes an attack. Its use has a specific rules outcome and should not be confused with simply lighting a traveling candle or freely manipulating fire.

It suits a straightforward magical attack without the special additional conditions listed for more advanced spells. However, damage is not determined by the spell's name or the size of the flame described in the story; it is calculated against the target's magical defense. Choosing an opponent and being able to see them remain important, and casting does not automatically cause further repeated burning.

Exact effect: Make a magical attack. Damage is calculated using the standard formula against the target's MDEF. Bonus: +1 to MATK. Target: 1 target within sight. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: —. Using it requires at least Intelligence 6, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/ohen/ohniva-strela.name: Fire Bolt
profile: Fire Bolt focuses a fire attack on a single target within sight. In a story, it can be a clear, swift expression of the caster's resolve. It is intended for a direct confrontation, rather than extending an explosion to everyone nearby. Its bonus distinguishes its effectiveness from the basic Spark, while the usual rules for a magical attack still apply.

It is useful when a hero wants to attack a specific opponent they can see. The final damage depends on the attack and the target's magical defense; it is not a fixed, guaranteed amount. The spell does not add unlisted hits on neighboring creatures or an ongoing burning condition. For the party, it can serve as a precisely aimed tool instead of a riskier area attack.

Exact effect: A direct, single-target magical fire attack against the target's MDEF. Bonus: +2 to MATK. Target: 1 target within sight. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: —. Using it requires at least Intelligence 7, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/ohen/zhavy-dotek.name: Searing Touch
profile: Searing Touch is a stronger fire attack that requires immediate proximity to the target. It suits a caster willing to take a risk to use greater offensive power. Its appearance in the story may be brief and intense, but it remains a specific magical attack, rather than continuous heat lasting through the next scene.

The decisive restriction is arm's reach: the caster must stand immediately beside the opponent. Planning therefore depends on the ability to approach safely and on nearby threats. The spell itself does not move the hero to the target or provide protection from retaliation. The higher bonus thus offers an interesting choice between attacking power and personal danger.

Exact effect: A stronger attack balanced by requiring touch; damage is determined against MDEF. Bonus: +3 to MATK. Target: 1 target within arm's reach. Duration: instantaneous. Restrictions: the caster must stand immediately beside the target. Using it requires at least Intelligence 8, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.

magic/ohen/kourova-clona.name: Smoke Screen
profile: Smoke Screen turns a small part of the battlefield into an area that is harder to attack through. Its value lies in shaping the encounter, aiding a retreat, or creating a brief opportunity to change position. It does not provide selective protection only for friends: the penalty applies to attacks from both sides if they pass through the screen.

Before casting, it helps to agree on where the party needs to move and from where it will continue attacking. A poorly placed screen can complicate the party's own plan. It lasts briefly and can be used only once per combat, so timing carries real weight. The catalog does not grant it automatic damage, complete invisibility, or the ability to remove every way an enemy could act.

Exact effect: Attacks made through the screen take −2 to their final PATK or MATK. The penalty applies to both sides. Target: an area approximately 3 m wide. Duration: 2 rounds. Restrictions: once per combat. Using it requires at least Intelligence 7, the appropriate casting ability, and knowledge of this spell. Meeting the numerical requirements alone does not grant knowledge of the spell.
